sentences.zh: 我凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 七十年的太空探索。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的球队。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界，并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受特别优惠，网址：nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日简报》。

sentences.en: As President Trump issues executive orders that encroach on the powers of Congress and in some cases fly in the face of established law,
sentences.zh: 随着特朗普总统发布行政命令，侵犯国会权力，并在某些情况下公然违背既定法律，

sentences.en: a debate has begun about whether he's merely testing the boundaries of his power or triggering a full-blown constitutional crisis.
sentences.zh: 一场关于他究竟是在试探权力边界，还是在引发一场全面宪政危机的辩论已经开始。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Adam Liptak wades through that debate.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事亚当·利普塔克将深入探讨这场辩论。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, February 12th.
sentences.zh: 今天是2月12日，星期三。

sentences.en: Tonight, there are warnings that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 今晚，有警告称美国

sentences.en: is dangerously close to a constitutional crisis.
sentences.zh: 正处于宪政危机的边缘，情况十分危险。

sentences.en: We are hearing the phrase constitutional crisis already less than a month into this presidency.
sentences.zh: 在这届总统任期开始不到一个月的时间里，我们已经听到了“宪政危机”这个词。

sentences.en: We've got our toes right on the edge.
sentences.zh: 我们已经站在了悬崖边上。

sentences.en: We are basically on the cusp.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上正处于临界点。

sentences.en: We're really heading toward a
sentences.zh: 我们真的正在走向一场

sentences.en: Constitutional
sentences.zh: 宪政

sentences.en: Constitutional
sentences.zh: 宪政

sentences.en: Constitutional crisis
sentences.zh: 宪政危机

sentences.en: Crisis
sentences.zh: 危机

sentences.en: Crisis
sentences.zh: 危机

sentences.en: Our founding fathers created three co-equal branches of government to ensure that no one man can be king.
sentences.zh: 我们的开国元勋建立了三个平等的政府分支，以确保没有人能成为国王。

sentences.en: But here we are.
sentences.zh: 但看看我们现在的情况。

sentences.en: Listen, I think this is the most serious constitutional crisis the country has faced.
sentences.zh: 听着，我认为这是这个国家面临的最严重的宪政危机。

sentences.en: Certainly since Watergate, the president.
sentences.zh: 当然，自水门事件以来，总统。

sentences.en: I can't tell you how many times I heard constitutional crisis during the first term of Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我无法告诉你，在唐纳德·特朗普的第一任期内，我听到了多少次“宪政危机”。

sentences.en: And here they go again.
sentences.zh: 他们又来了。

sentences.en: Welcome back.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回来。

sentences.en: Always a distinct pleasure.
sentences.zh: 总是非常荣幸。

sentences.en: It's good to be here, Michael.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里，迈克尔。

sentences.en: The phrase du jour, Adam, right now in Washington is constitutional crisis.
sentences.zh: 亚当，现在华盛顿最流行的词就是“宪政危机”。

sentences.en: And we come to you as our resident scholar of the law and the courts to understand what a constitutional crisis actually is and how you know when you are in the middle of one.
sentences.zh: 我们请你这位法律和法院领域的常驻学者来解释一下，什么是真正的宪政危机，以及如何判断自己是否正身处其中。

sentences.en: Yeah, it sounds serious, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 是啊，听起来很严重，不是吗？

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But I've been talking to a lot of law professors and what emerges from those conversations is that there's no fixed agreed upon definition of a constitutional crisis.
sentences.zh: 但我一直在和许多法学教授交谈，从这些谈话中得出的结论是，对于宪政危机，并没有一个固定的、公认的定义。

sentences.en: It has characteristics, notably when one of the three branches tries to get out of its lane, assert too much power.
sentences.zh: 它有一些特征，特别是在三个分支中的一个试图越权、主张过多权力时。

sentences.en: It often involves a president flouting statutes, flouting the Constitution, flouting judicial orders.
sentences.zh: 它通常涉及总统蔑视法规、蔑视宪法、蔑视司法命令。

sentences.en: And it can be a single instance, but it's more typically cumulative.
sentences.zh: 它可以是一个单一的事件，但通常是累积性的。

sentences.en: But it's not a binary thing.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是非黑即白的。

sentences.en: It's not a switch.
sentences.zh: 它不是一个开关。

sentences.en: It's a slope that can descend.
sentences.zh: 它是一个可能会不断下滑的斜坡。

sentences.en: And it takes on a quality of danger if there's a lot of it.
sentences.zh: 如果这种情况发生得很多，它就会带有一种危险的性质。

sentences.en: So, given that loose definition that seems to acknowledge the fluidity of a constitutional crisis,
sentences.zh: 那么，考虑到这个似乎承认宪政危机流动性的宽泛定义，

sentences.en: how should we think about whether President Trump's actions over the past few weeks represent a constitutional crisis or perhaps something else, something less serious?
sentences.zh: 我们应该如何看待特朗普总统过去几周的行为是否代表了一场宪政危机，或者也许是其他什么东西，一些不那么严重的事情？

sentences.en: So, the consensus is that this is a constitutional crisis.
sentences.zh: 所以，目前的共识是，这是一场宪政危机。

sentences.en: And let me try to unpack why so many people think that.
sentences.zh: 让我试着剖析一下为什么这么多人会这样认为。

sentences.en: The president will often use his power to its fullest extent to assert a constitutional authority to do things that other branches may oppose.
sentences.zh: 总统经常会最大限度地利用他的权力，以主张一种宪法权威，去做其他分支可能反对的事情。

sentences.en: But what we have with President Trump is a kind of wholesale reconception of the part of the Constitution, Article 2, that sets out presidential power,
sentences.zh: 但特朗普总统所做的是对宪法中规定总统权力的第二条进行了一种全面的重新构想，

sentences.en: that asserts that he's basically the decision maker, that he can act alone.
sentences.zh: 他声称自己基本上是决策者，他可以单独行动。

sentences.en: He can disregard instructions from Congress.
sentences.zh: 他可以无视国会的指示。

sentences.en: And Congress is in Article 1.
sentences.zh: 而国会是在第一条中规定的。

sentences.en: Congress makes the law.
sentences.zh: 国会制定法律。

sentences.en: That sounds significant.
sentences.zh: 这听起来意义重大。

sentences.en: The president is charged by the Constitution to take care that the laws be faithfully executed.
sentences.zh: 宪法赋予总统职责，确保法律得到忠实执行。

sentences.en: That would seem ordinarily to put him in a subordinate role.
sentences.zh: 这通常似乎会让他处于从属地位。

sentences.en: But the music of Trump's actions over the past several weeks has been quite different, has meant to insist on his primacy.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普过去几周行动的基调却截然不同，意在坚持他的至高无上。

sentences.en: Adam, walk us through some of the specific examples of how President Trump is muddling with our traditional notions of Article 1, Article 2.
sentences.zh: 亚当，请带我们了解一些具体的例子，看看特朗普总统是如何混淆我们对第一条和第二条的传统认知的。

sentences.en: Basically, the separation of powers between the legislative and executive branch and how he is trying to expand the powers of the executive.
sentences.zh: 基本上，就是立法分支和行政分支之间的权力分立，以及他如何试图扩大行政权力。

sentences.en: So a couple of quick examples.
sentences.zh: 举几个简单的例子。

sentences.en: Congress has instructed the president not to fire people unless he satisfies certain criteria.
sentences.zh: 国会已指示总统，除非满足特定标准，否则不得解雇人员。

sentences.en: Sometimes he has to have a good reason.
sentences.zh: 有时他必须有正当理由。

sentences.en: Sometimes he has to wait 30 days.
sentences.zh: 有时他必须等待30天。

sentences.en: Sometimes he has to explain himself to Congress.
sentences.zh: 有时他必须向国会解释。

sentences.en: President Trump has busted through all those limitations and insisted that as head of the executive branch, he can fire whomever he will.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统打破了所有这些限制，并坚持认为作为行政部门的首脑，他可以随意解雇任何人。

sentences.en: Congress has also passed laws instructing the president to spend money to do certain things.
sentences.zh: 国会还通过了法律，指示总统花钱去做某些事情。

sentences.en: President Trump takes the view that if those instructions are inconsistent with his policy agenda, he doesn't have to do it.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统认为，如果这些指示与他的政策议程不一致，他就不必执行。

sentences.en: That Congress can't make him spend the money Congress has appropriated.
sentences.zh: 国会不能强迫他花费国会拨款的钱。

sentences.en: And Congress, of course, has the power of the purse.
sentences.zh: 当然，国会拥有钱袋子权力。

sentences.en: So you would think there's a pretty good argument that the president has to do with Congress says.
sentences.zh: 所以你会认为，总统必须按照国会说的去做，这个论点很有力。

sentences.en: So, for example, what you just said would apply to the congressionally appropriated money for USAID, the foreign aid agency that the president has decided to shut down.
sentences.zh: 那么，举个例子，你刚才说的适用于国会为美国国际开发署（USAID）拨款的资金，而总统决定关闭该机构。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Congress told the president what to do.
sentences.zh: 国会告诉总统该怎么做。

sentences.en: The president is doing the opposite.
sentences.zh: 总统却反其道而行之。

sentences.en: That seems to contain some real seeds of what most people would think of as a constitutional crisis.
sentences.zh: 这似乎包含了一些大多数人认为的宪政危机的真正种子。

sentences.en: And this is notable, too, Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，这一点也很值得注意。

sentences.en: He's doing this in the face of a Congress that's not opposing him.
sentences.zh: 他是在一个并不反对他的国会面前这样做。

sentences.en: To the contrary, if President Trump were to seek legislation from this Congress limiting or shutting down USAID, I think he'd be very likely to succeed.
sentences.zh: 相反，如果特朗普总统寻求本届国会立法限制或关闭美国国际开发署，我认为他很有可能会成功。

sentences.en: But he seems not to be interested in working with the other branch, a branch that he essentially controls, but to insist that he has the sole power to do things.
sentences.zh: 但他似乎对与另一个分支合作不感兴趣，尽管他基本上控制着那个分支，但他坚持认为自己拥有做事的唯一权力。

sentences.en: So what might deepen the sense that we are in a constitutional crisis is not just that the president is ignoring Congress's will, its actions, its appropriations.
sentences.zh: 所以，加深我们正处于宪政危机感的原因，不仅是总统无视国会的意愿、行动和拨款，

sentences.en: But he's not even engaging them on these questions in a way that he very much could.
sentences.zh: 而且他甚至没有以他完全可以做到的方式在这些问题上与他们接触。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a raw assertion of power.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一种赤裸裸的权力主张。

sentences.en: And it's a little surprising.
sentences.zh: 而且有点令人惊讶。

sentences.en: I mean, if you have a Republican-controlled Congress that's ready to do your bidding and you could button this down and make lasting change that's unassailable,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你有一个共和党控制的国会准备听从你的指挥，你可以把这件事定下来，做出持久且不可动摇的改变，

sentences.en: it's a little bit surprising that in the early weeks of a four-year term, he wants to do everything at once.
sentences.zh: 在四年任期的最初几周内，他想一次性做完所有事情，这有点令人惊讶。

sentences.en: And that has the quality of a crisis, too.
sentences.zh: 这也具有危机的性质。

sentences.en: This notion that we're flooding the zone with endless executive orders and scores of lawsuits,
sentences.zh: 这种用无休止的行政命令和大量诉讼淹没该领域的想法，

sentences.en: it just gives rise to the sense that we're encountering a wholly new and maybe dangerous atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 只会让人觉得我们正在遭遇一种全新的、也许是危险的氛围。

sentences.en: Well, where else do his actions seem to potentially be creating a constitutional crisis?
sentences.zh: 那么，他的行为还在哪些方面似乎有可能造成宪政危机？

sentences.en: So where to begin?
sentences.zh: 从何说起呢？

sentences.en: He has shut down all kinds of federal spending that Congress has instructed him to spend.
sentences.zh: 他已经停止了国会指示他支出的各种联邦支出。

sentences.en: He's deputized Elon Musk and his Doge warriors to inspect all kinds of government logs and computer activity that gives rise to at least some privacy concerns.
sentences.zh: 他授权埃隆·马斯克和他的“政府效率部”战士去检查各种政府日志和计算机活动，这至少引起了一些隐私担忧。

sentences.en: And maybe notably, he has, by executive order, purported to do away with what is generally thought to be a fundamental constitutional right of birthright citizenship.
sentences.zh: 也许值得注意的是，他通过行政命令，声称要废除通常被认为是出生公民权这一基本宪法权利的东西。

sentences.en: That is, with very rare exceptions.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，除了极少数例外。

sentences.en: If you're born in the United States, you're a United States citizen.
sentences.zh: 如果你出生在美国，你就是美国公民。

sentences.en: And that list of actions that you just went through, it feels like they aren't all the same.
sentences.zh: 你刚才列举的那些行动，感觉它们并不完全一样。

sentences.en: So which ones, in your mind and in the mind of the legal scholars that you're speaking to,
sentences.zh: 那么在你看来，以及在你交谈过的法律学者看来，哪些行动

sentences.en: are just the president seeking to expand his authority, which we've always understood President Trump to want to do, even during the campaign?
sentences.zh: 只是总统试图扩大他的权力，我们一直认为特朗普总统想这样做，即使在竞选期间也是如此？

sentences.en: And which ones seem like, you know, just frontal assaults on the Constitution and potentially the stuff of a constitutional crisis?
sentences.zh: 而哪些看起来像是对宪法的正面攻击，并且可能是宪政危机的素材？

sentences.en: So I think I'd put it in three buckets, Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我想我会把它们分为三类。

sentences.en: One is Trump's role as the head of the executive branch.
sentences.zh: 第一类是特朗普作为行政部门首脑的角色。

sentences.en: And there, he has pretty good arguments that he's the boss, that he can decide who works for him,
sentences.zh: 在那里，他有很好的论据证明他是老板，他可以决定谁为他工作，

sentences.en: and that he can fire people, including heads of independent agencies that Congress has tried to insulate from political pressure,
sentences.zh: 他可以解雇人员，包括国会试图使其免受政治压力的独立机构的负责人，

sentences.en: inspectors general, who have an important role in keeping fraud and corruption out of agencies.
sentences.zh: 以及在防止机构欺诈和腐败方面发挥重要作用的监察长。

sentences.en: That may not sound like the best idea as a policy matter.
sentences.zh: 从政策角度来看，这听起来可能不是最好的主意。

sentences.en: But the Supreme Court has been increasingly sympathetic to the idea that, at least where it's all inside the executive branch, the president has a lot of power.
sentences.zh: 但最高法院越来越同情这样一种观点，即至少在行政部门内部，总统拥有很大的权力。

sentences.en: So that first bucket, he may well succeed in many of his arguments.
sentences.zh: 所以第一类，他的许多论点很可能会成功。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He has a legal leg to stand on.
sentences.zh: 他有法律依据。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The second bucket gets much harder, where Congress has specifically instructed him to do something,
sentences.zh: 第二类就困难多了，国会明确指示他做某事，

sentences.en: to spend money, to maintain agencies, USAID, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, the Department of Education.
sentences.zh: 比如花钱、维持机构，如美国国际开发署、消费者金融保护局、教育部。

sentences.en: The notion that the president is allowed to disregard congressional instructions on things like that, that's a tough argument.
sentences.zh: 总统被允许无视国会在这些事情上的指示，这种观点很难站得住脚。

sentences.en: And then the third bucket gets even harder, where the Constitution, most people think, has insisted that there's a constitutional right to birthright citizenship.
sentences.zh: 然后第三类就更难了，大多数人认为宪法坚持存在出生公民权的宪法权利。

sentences.en: And under the conventional understanding, you can't do away with that by executive order.
sentences.zh: 按照传统的理解，你不能通过行政命令废除它。

sentences.en: You can't do away with that by statute.
sentences.zh: 你不能通过法规废除它。

sentences.en: Congress can't do away with it.
sentences.zh: 国会也不能废除它。

sentences.en: It's in the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 它写在宪法里。

sentences.en: If something's going to change, it needs to be done by constitutional amendment.
sentences.zh: 如果有什么要改变，需要通过宪法修正案来完成。

sentences.en: So the president's order in the early days of his administration that says, I declare that this constitutional right doesn't exist, is quite brazen and bold.
sentences.zh: 所以总统在执政初期发布的命令说，我宣布这种宪法权利不存在，这是相当厚颜无耻和大胆的。

sentences.en: So now that we know that Congress does not seem inclined to act against this president, the Republican-controlled House and Senate,
sentences.zh: 既然我们知道国会似乎不倾向于反对这位总统，即共和党控制的众议院和参议院，

sentences.en: and given that the president doesn't seem all that interested in engaging this Congress,
sentences.zh: 而且考虑到总统似乎对与本届国会接触并不感兴趣，

sentences.en: it very much does seem like we're at a point where, if we are, as these scholars have told you,
sentences.zh: 这确实看起来我们正处于一个时刻，如果正如这些学者告诉你的那样，

sentences.en: in a constitutional crisis of one form or another, that it will be the courts, the federal courts, that will play a major role in keeping the president in check.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于某种形式的宪政危机中，那么将是法院，即联邦法院，在制衡总统方面发挥重要作用。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the courts are already dealing with an extraordinary number of suits.
sentences.zh: 法院已经在处理数量惊人的诉讼。

sentences.en: They seem to multiply by the day.
sentences.zh: 它们似乎每天都在增加。

sentences.en: And while none of them have reached the Supreme Court yet, in the coming, I would say, weeks, we are going to have major clashes before a Supreme Court that, you know,
sentences.zh: 虽然还没有任何诉讼到达最高法院，但我认为在接下来的几周里，我们将会在最高法院面前发生重大冲突，你知道，

sentences.en: is dominated by six conservative appointees and will be sympathetic to some of what Trump wants to achieve, but is not going to be on board for the whole project.
sentences.zh: 最高法院由六名保守派任命的法官主导，他们会同情特朗普想要实现的部分目标，但不会支持整个计划。

sentences.en: And then the open question is, assuming the court rules against President Trump, will he obey that judgment?
sentences.zh: 那么悬而未决的问题是，假设法院裁定特朗普总统败诉，他会服从判决吗？

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《纽约时报》游戏中的拼图游戏之一《Connections》，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尝试捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人那样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 开始游戏吧。

sentences.en: Adam, so far, it is not the Supreme Court, as you said, but the lower federal courts that have weighed in on President Trump's actions.
sentences.zh: 亚当，到目前为止，正如你所说，并不是最高法院，而是下级联邦法院对特朗普总统的行为发表了意见。

sentences.en: And my sense is that so far, they have taken a very dim view of his efforts to expand his executive power and encroach on the powers of Congress.
sentences.zh: 我的感觉是，到目前为止，他们对总统试图扩大行政权力、侵犯国会权力的做法持非常不赞成的态度。

sentences.en: He has been on an epic losing streak.
sentences.zh: 他最近一直在经历一连串的惨败。

sentences.en: Some of that can be explained by plaintiffs suing in friendly courts, but appointees of all different kinds of presidents, including President Trump himself,
sentences.zh: 部分原因可以解释为原告在友好的法院提起诉讼，但各种不同总统任命的法官，包括特朗普总统本人任命的法官，

sentences.en: have ruled against him and have said that Elon Musk can't have access to some materials, that people can't be fired, that agencies can't be disassembled,
sentences.zh: 都做出了对他不利的裁决，并表示埃隆·马斯克不能获取某些材料，不能随意解雇员工，不能解散政府机构，

sentences.en: that the birthright citizenship order is unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 并称出生公民权行政令违宪。

sentences.en: And some of these judges have been very harsh.
sentences.zh: 而且其中一些法官的措辞非常严厉。

sentences.en: One of them, in blocking the birthright citizenship order, said that he had difficulty understanding how a member of the bar
sentences.zh: 其中一位法官在阻止出生公民权行政令时表示，他很难理解一名律师

sentences.en: could state unequivocally that this is a constitutional order.
sentences.zh: 怎么能断言这是一项合宪的行政令。

sentences.en: It boggles my mind.
sentences.zh: 这简直让我无法理解。

sentences.en: So that gives you a flavor of how Trump is doing in the lower courts.
sentences.zh: 所以，这让你了解了特朗普在下级法院的处境。

sentences.en: And, of course, this has prompted some around the president to say, well, hold on a minute.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也促使总统身边的一些人说，等等，先别急。

sentences.en: The courts are overstepping their bounds in reigning in our efforts to expand our bounds.
sentences.zh: 法院在限制我们扩大权力的努力方面越界了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And J.D.
sentences.zh: 而副总统万斯

sentences.en: Vance, the vice president, has taken the most assertive attitude toward this, saying that the president doesn't have to obey rulings from courts
sentences.zh: 对此采取了最强硬的态度，称总统不必服从那些

sentences.en: that are at odds with his understanding of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 与他对宪法理解相抵触的法院裁决。

sentences.en: I just want to read what J.D.
sentences.zh: 我只想读一下万斯

sentences.en: Vance wrote about this, because he tried to put it into a larger legal context.
sentences.zh: 对此写的内容，因为他试图将其置于更大的法律背景下。

sentences.en: And he seemed to write this right after the president had lost a series of rulings of the kind you just went through.
sentences.zh: 他似乎是在总统刚刚输掉你刚才提到的那一连串官司后写下的这些话。

sentences.en: And he wrote, if a judge tried to tell a general how to conduct a military operation, that would be illegal.
sentences.zh: 他写道，如果法官试图告诉将军如何进行军事行动，那将是非法的。

sentences.en: And he goes on to say, if a judge tried to command the attorney general in how to use her discretion as a prosecutor, that would be illegal.
sentences.zh: 他接着说，如果法官试图指挥司法部长如何行使检察官的自由裁量权，那也是非法的。

sentences.en: And then he goes on to apply this logic to the president.
sentences.zh: 然后他继续将这一逻辑应用到总统身上。

sentences.en: He says, judges aren't allowed to control the executive's legitimate power either.
sentences.zh: 他说，法官也不允许控制行政部门的合法权力。

sentences.en: So what do we make of that argument?
sentences.zh: 那么我们该如何看待这一论点呢？

sentences.en: So it sounds quite radical, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 听起来很激进，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, we generally agree as Americans that the court has the last word over the constitutionality of congressional action, executive action.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，作为美国人，我们通常同意法院对国会行为和行政行为的合宪性拥有最终决定权。

sentences.en: And if J.D.
sentences.zh: 如果万斯

sentences.en: Vance is suggesting as a general matter that the president disagrees with that, well, that's a constitutional crisis.
sentences.zh: 从总体上暗示总统不同意这一点，那么，这就是一场宪政危机。

sentences.en: I guess I would make, though, an observation, Michael, that there are probably some areas where if the constitution distinctly and exclusively
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我想我得观察到，可能在某些领域，如果宪法明确且排他性地

sentences.en: commits some right to the president, like, say, the pardon power, and a court were to say, no, you can't pardon your buddy,
sentences.zh: 赋予总统某种权利，比如赦免权，而法院却说，不，你不能赦免你的哥们儿，

sentences.en: the president's interpretation of the constitution could well govern there.
sentences.zh: 那么总统对宪法的解释很可能在那里起主导作用。

sentences.en: And there's a flavor of this in the Supreme Court's decision in July granting Trump broad immunity from prosecution, where the court talks about those powers that are core
sentences.zh: 最高法院七月份授予特朗普广泛的起诉豁免权的裁决中就带有这种意味，法院谈到了那些核心的

sentences.en: executive powers are for the president only.
sentences.zh: 行政权力仅属于总统。

sentences.en: The Vance statement seems to resonate with that way of thinking, too.
sentences.zh: 万斯的声明似乎也与这种思维方式产生了共鸣。

sentences.en: In other words, it may be a narrower interpretation of when the president can ignore the courts than perhaps it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这可能比看起来更狭义地解释了总统何时可以无视法院。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I don't want to minimize it.
sentences.zh: 但我不想淡化它。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a hell of a thing to even contemplate the Supreme Court saying to Richard Nixon, you've got to turn over the White House tapes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最高法院对理查德·尼克松说“你必须交出白宫录音带”，这本身就是一件了不得的事情。

sentences.en: And Richard Nixon, and he thought about this, saying no.
sentences.zh: 而理查德·尼克松——他确实考虑过——却说不。

sentences.en: That would be a classic constitutional crisis.
sentences.zh: 那将是一场典型的宪政危机。

sentences.en: Well, what Vance is writing here seems to presuppose that there's going to come a moment
sentences.zh: 嗯，万斯在这里写的似乎预设了这样一个时刻即将到来：

sentences.en: pretty soon when these lower court rulings get appealed all the way up to the Supreme Court,
sentences.zh: 很快，这些下级法院的裁决就会一路上诉到最高法院，

sentences.en: and the Supreme Court issues a ruling against President Trump that attempts to rein in his power.
sentences.zh: 而最高法院会做出不利于特朗普总统的裁决，试图限制他的权力。

sentences.en: And I guess I'm curious, based on your legal analysis and your reporting over the past couple of weeks,
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，根据你的法律分析和你过去几周的报道，

sentences.en: where we think the Supreme Court may choose to weigh in and attempt to curtail the president's power.
sentences.zh: 你认为最高法院可能会在什么地方介入并试图削弱总统的权力。

sentences.en: We don't know, of course, exactly what case will reach the court and exactly how the court will think about it.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们不知道具体会有什么案件到达法院，也不知道法院会如何考虑它。

sentences.en: I think the court will be very scared of, alert to the possibility of a constitutional crisis, of a pure impasse.
sentences.zh: 我认为法院会非常害怕，并警惕宪政危机或纯粹僵局的可能性。

sentences.en: So my guess, Michael, is that the court is going to try to find a case where, in a splashy way,
sentences.zh: 所以迈克尔，我的猜测是，法院会试图找一个案件，以一种引人注目的方式，

sentences.en: it rebukes Trump, rules against him, but ideally in a case where the president can't really disobey the court's judgment.
sentences.zh: 谴责特朗普，做出对他不利的裁决，但最好是在一个总统无法真正违抗法院判决的案件中。

sentences.en: And birthright citizenship is the classic example of this.
sentences.zh: 而出生公民权就是这方面的典型例子。

sentences.en: And why would the court think that Trump could not, even if he wanted to, disobey that ruling?
sentences.zh: 为什么法院会认为特朗普即使想违抗该裁决也做不到呢？

sentences.en: It's just a logistical nightmare.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一场后勤噩梦。

sentences.en: It requires Trump to essentially instruct every hospital administrator in the nation about how to track the citizenship of every newborn.
sentences.zh: 它要求特朗普基本上指示全国每一位医院管理员如何追踪每个新生儿的公民身份。

sentences.en: It's hard enough to do, if you had the law at your back, in the face of a Supreme Court judgment, it becomes really hard to imagine.
sentences.zh: 这本身就很难做到，如果面对最高法院的判决，即便你有法律支持，也很难想象他能做到。

sentences.en: — I'm curious, Adam, what would be a case where the Supreme Court might fear that Trump would disobey them?
sentences.zh: ——亚当，我很好奇，有没有什么案件是最高法院可能会担心特朗普会违抗他们的？

sentences.en: A pretty staggering thing to contemplate.
sentences.zh: 这真是令人震惊的设想。

sentences.en: But from what you're saying, the court actively does fear that.
sentences.zh: 但从你的话来看，法院确实在积极担心这一点。

sentences.en: — I guess I can think of lots of examples, but why don't we talk about USAID?
sentences.zh: ——我想我可以想到很多例子，但我们为什么不谈谈美国国际开发署（USAID）呢？

sentences.en: The president wants to do away with that.
sentences.zh: 总统想废除它。

sentences.en: The court says, you can't do that on your own.
sentences.zh: 法院说，你不能独自这样做。

sentences.en: You can go to Congress.
sentences.zh: 你可以去找国会。

sentences.en: But you are not authorized, Mr. President, to disobey Congress's instructions about the existence of and the nature of and the spending of that agency.
sentences.zh: 但总统先生，你无权违抗国会关于该机构的存在、性质和开支的指示。

sentences.en: And Trump, let's posit, says, I disagree, and shuts the agency down anyway.
sentences.zh: 假设特朗普说，我不同意，然后还是强行关闭了该机构。

sentences.en: The court doesn't want to find itself in that situation.
sentences.zh: 法院不想让自己陷入那种境地。

sentences.en: The court has always, through its entire history, been very sensitive to the idea that it's not really clear why we do what it tells us to do.
sentences.zh: 法院在整个历史上一直非常敏感，因为它并不真正清楚为什么人们会听从它的指令。

sentences.en: They don't have an army.
sentences.zh: 他们没有军队。

sentences.en: They don't have the power of the purse.
sentences.zh: 他们没有财政大权。

sentences.en: They have this kind of fuzzy thing we call legitimacy and authority.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有一种我们称之为合法性和权威的模糊东西。

sentences.en: And they're very wary of that being undermined.
sentences.zh: 他们非常担心这种东西被削弱。

sentences.en: And all it takes is for the president at one time to say, as Andrew Jackson did say, apocryphally, the chief justice has made his decision.
sentences.zh: 而总统只需要有一次像安德鲁·杰克逊那样说——尽管这可能是杜撰的——首席大法官已经做出了他的决定。

sentences.en: Now let him enforce it.
sentences.zh: 现在让他去执行吧。

sentences.en: — Right.
sentences.zh: ——没错。

sentences.en: You're saying the court's authority is a norm, and Trump likes to subvert norMs.
sentences.zh: 你是说法院的权威是一种准则，而特朗普喜欢颠覆准则。

sentences.en: And you think the court would go out of its way to avoid rulings, even when they are correct on the legal merits, that Trump might seek to subvert, which is pretty fascinating.
sentences.zh: 你认为法院会竭尽全力避免做出那些即使在法律上是正确的，但特朗普可能会试图颠覆的裁决，这真是太迷人了。

sentences.en: — I think you would get some motivated reasoning from justices who probably wouldn't put this at the forefront of their minds, but would talk themselves into thinking, well,
sentences.zh: ——我认为你会从大法官那里得到一些动机性推理，他们可能不会把这放在心头，但会说服自己认为，嗯，

sentences.en: maybe we rule for the president here.
sentences.zh: 也许我们在这里应该支持总统。

sentences.en: Maybe it's not such a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 也许这并不是什么坏事。

sentences.en: And somewhere, you know, in the substrata of their consciousness is the lurking feeling that if we go the other way, things are going to be bad for the institution.
sentences.zh: 在他们意识的底层，潜伏着一种感觉：如果我们走另一条路，事情对这个机构来说会很糟糕。

sentences.en: — So what we would seem to be looking at, Adam, based on everything you're saying,
sentences.zh: ——所以迈克尔，根据你所说的一切，我们似乎看到的是，

sentences.en: is a legislative branch that's not at all enthusiastic about curtailing the president's authority.
sentences.zh: 立法部门对限制总统权力一点也不热心。

sentences.en: We're looking at a judicial branch with the Supreme Court atop it that is disinclined to try to curtail the president's power out of fear that he may ultimately just ignore them.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是一个以最高法院为首的司法部门，由于担心总统最终可能会直接无视他们，而不愿试图限制总统的权力。

sentences.en: — And so it seems very possible that, as these legal scholars have told you, we may be in what they see as a constitutional crisis.
sentences.zh: ——所以正如那些法律学者告诉你的那样，我们可能正处于他们所认为的宪政危机之中，这似乎很有可能。

sentences.en: I guess my question is, what happens if we are in a constitutional crisis and most Americans don't care?
sentences.zh: 我的问题是，如果我们处于宪政危机中，而大多数美国人并不关心，那会怎样？

sentences.en: And I ask that because Trump was elected by tens of millions of people who wanted him to shake up the system.
sentences.zh: 我之所以这样问，是因为特朗普是由数千万希望他重塑体制的人选出来的。

sentences.en: And early polling does very much suggest that many people are pleased at the pace at which he's fulfilling his promises.
sentences.zh: 早期的民调确实非常强烈地表明，许多人对他在兑现承诺方面的进展感到满意。

sentences.en: And part of that promise was a stronger executive who's just busting through any barrier in his way.
sentences.zh: 而这些承诺的一部分就是一个更强大的行政首脑，能够冲破阻碍他的一切障碍。

sentences.en: And so is it a constitutional crisis if a lot of Americans don't see it as a crisis?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果很多美国人并不认为这是一场危机，那它还是宪政危机吗？

sentences.en: — It can be thought of, and I take your point, as simply a reimagining of what the Constitution calls for that maybe people approve of.
sentences.zh: ——可以这样想，我明白你的意思，这可能只是对宪法要求的重新构想，也许人们对此表示赞同。

sentences.en: And maybe what we're on the cusp of here is, you know, without an amendment, without a constitutional convention,
sentences.zh: 也许我们正处于这样一个关口，你知道，在没有修正案、没有制宪会议的情况下，

sentences.en: just a reorientation of the separation of powers in a way that elevates the president to a role that we've not seen before at the expense of the other branches.
sentences.zh: 只是对权力分立进行了重新定位，以牺牲其他部门为代价，将总统提升到了一个我们从未见过的角色。

sentences.en: — But all of that said, a crisis is a crisis.
sentences.zh: ——但话虽如此，危机就是危机。

sentences.en: And if our very understanding of the Constitution is being tested by a president who legal scholars say seems to have a contempt for the document,
sentences.zh: 如果法律学者所说的对宪法怀有蔑视的总统正在考验我们对宪法的理解，

sentences.en: we are in the midst of something profound, whether or not people are taking it seriously today.
sentences.zh: 那么无论人们今天是否认真对待，我们都正处于某种深刻变革之中。

sentences.en: — Well, Adam, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: ——好吧，亚当，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: — Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: ——谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: — On Tuesday night, President Trump personally denounced the federal judges who have blocked his actions over the past few weeks,
sentences.zh: ——周二晚上，特朗普总统亲自谴责了过去几周阻止他行动的联邦法官，

sentences.en: especially his attempts to shut down agencies like USAID and freeze their funds.
sentences.zh: 特别是他试图关闭像美国国际开发署这样的机构并冻结其资金的尝试。

sentences.en: — And it seems hard to believe that judges want to try and stop us from looking for corruption, especially when we found hundreds of millions of dollars worth, much more than that,
sentences.zh: ——很难相信法官们想要阻止我们调查腐败，尤其是当我们发现了价值数亿美元，甚至远不止这些的腐败时，

sentences.en: in just a short period of time.
sentences.zh: 而且是在很短的时间内发现的。

sentences.en: — And he delivered what appeared to be a thinly veiled threat against the judges, who stand in his way.
sentences.zh: ——他发表了似乎是对阻碍他的法官们含蓄的威胁。

sentences.en: — Well, so maybe we have to look at the judges, because that's a very serious, I think it's a very serious violation.
sentences.zh: ——好吧，所以也许我们必须审视一下这些法官，因为我认为这是一个非常严重的违规行为。

sentences.en: — We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: ——我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: — During an extraordinary 30-minute appearance in the Oval Office on Tuesday night, Elon Musk, joined by his four-year-old son,
sentences.zh: ——周二晚上，埃隆·马斯克在椭圆形办公室进行了一次非同寻常的30分钟露面，他四岁的儿子也陪同在侧，

sentences.en: defended his plans to drastically shrink the size of the federal government.
sentences.zh: 为他大幅缩减联邦政府规模的计划进行了辩护。

sentences.en: — We have this unelected, fourth unconstitutional branch of government, which is the bureaucracy, which has, in a lot of ways, currently more power than any elected representative.
sentences.zh: ——我们有这个未经选举的、第四个违宪的政府分支，也就是官僚机构，在很多方面，它目前比任何民选代表拥有更大的权力。

sentences.en: And this is not something that people want.
sentences.zh: 这不是人们想要的。

sentences.en: — But Musk made multiple unsubstantiated claims about government fraud, including the claim that officials at USAID have taken kickbacks.
sentences.zh: ——但马斯克对政府欺诈提出了多项未经证实的指控，包括声称美国国际开发署的官员收受了回扣。

sentences.en: And he acknowledged that some of his most inflammatory public claims — for instance, that aid workers planned to send $50 million worth of condoms to Hamas — were wrong.
sentences.zh: 他也承认他一些最煽动性的公开言论——例如，援助人员计划向哈马斯运送价值5000万美元的避孕套——是错误的。

sentences.en: — Well, first of all, some of the things that I say will be incorrect and should be corrected, so nobody's going to bat a thousand.
sentences.zh: ——嗯，首先，我所说的一些事情是不正确的，应该予以纠正，所以没有人能保证百分之百正确。

sentences.en: I mean, any — you know, we will make mistakes, but we'll act quickly to correct any mistakes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，任何——你知道，我们会犯错，但我们会迅速采取行动纠正任何错误。

sentences.en: — And during a visit to the White House, King Abdullah of Jordan rejected President Trump's proposal that his country take in Palestinians living in Gaza.
sentences.zh: ——在访问白宫期间，约旦国王阿卜杜拉拒绝了特朗普总统关于其国家接收居住在加沙的巴勒斯坦人的提议。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, Trump reiterated his plan for the United States to take over Gaza through unspecified means,
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，特朗普重申了他的计划，即美国通过未指明的手段接管加沙，

sentences.en: and for Jordan and Egypt to accept Palestinians who would be permanently displaced as the U.S.
sentences.zh: 并让约旦和埃及接收那些在美方

sentences.en: redevelops the territory.
sentences.zh: 重新开发该领土时将被永久流离失所的巴勒斯坦人。

sentences.en: — This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: ——本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: — Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: ——他们是那种需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是指他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
